questions.stem: An arithmetic sequence is one in which:
options: each term is the sum of the two terms that come before it
the terms increase by a larger amount each time they grow
the same number is added to each term to get the next term
each term is multiplied by the same number to get the next
questions.explanation: An arithmetic sequence has a common difference d added at every step, so it grows or decays by a constant amount. Multiplying by the same number each time gives a geometric sequence.

questions.stem: For the arithmetic sequence 7, 11, 15, 19, ..., the common difference is:
questions.explanation: The common difference is any term minus the term before it: 11 − 7 = 4. Dividing 11 by 7 gives about 1.57, which would be a common ratio, and this sequence does not have one.

questions.stem: A sequence is defined by tₙ₊₁ = tₙ − 6, t₁ = 50. The value of t₄ is:
questions.explanation: Applying the rule three times: t₂ = 44, t₃ = 38, t₄ = 32. Subtracting 6 four times gives 26, which is t₅, an off-by-one slip.

questions.stem: The rule for the nth term of an arithmetic sequence with first term t₁ and common difference d is:
questions.explanation: The first term has had no differences added, the second one, and the nth term has had n − 1 of them, so tₙ = t₁ + (n − 1)d. tₙ = t₁dⁿ⁻¹ is the shape of the geometric rule.

questions.stem: For the arithmetic sequence 7, 11, 15, 19, ..., the 10th term is:
questions.explanation: t₁₀ = 7 + (10 − 1) × 4 = 7 + 36 = 43. Using n instead of n − 1 gives 7 + 40 = 47, one difference too many.

questions.stem: The nth-term rule for the arithmetic sequence 20, 17, 14, 11, ... is:
questions.explanation: Here t₁ = 20 and d = −3, so tₙ = 20 + (n − 1)(−3) = 20 − 3(n − 1). The rule tₙ = 20 − 3n gives t₁ = 17, so it starts one term too late.

questions.stem: An arithmetic sequence has t₁ = 5 and t₈ = 40. The common difference is:
questions.explanation: t₈ = t₁ + 7d, so 40 = 5 + 7d, giving 7d = 35 and d = 5. Dividing 35 by 8 instead of 7 gives 4.375, which miscounts the number of steps.

questions.stem: In the arithmetic sequence 3, 7, 11, 15, ..., which term is equal to 99?
questions.explanation: Solve 3 + (n − 1) × 4 = 99: (n − 1) × 4 = 96, so n − 1 = 24 and n = 25. Stopping at n − 1 = 24 gives the 24th term, which is 95.

questions.stem: An arithmetic sequence has t₃ = 17 and t₇ = 33. The first term, t₁, is:
questions.explanation: From t₃ to t₇ is 4 steps, so 4d = 33 − 17 = 16 and d = 4. Then t₁ = t₃ − 2d = 17 − 8 = 9. Subtracting only one difference from t₃ gives 13, which is t₂.

questions.stem: When the terms of an arithmetic sequence are graphed against the term number, the points:
options: lie on a curve that gets steeper and steeper
lie on a curve that flattens towards zero
lie on a straight line through the origin
lie on a straight line and are not joined
questions.explanation: Each step changes the value by the same amount, so the points lie in a straight line, which is linear growth or decay. They are discrete points, one per term, so they are not joined; the line need not pass through the origin.

questions.stem: A taxi fare is a flag fall of $3.20 plus $2.10 per kilometre. The fare for a 12 km trip is:
questions.explanation: Fare = 3.20 + 12 × 2.10 = 3.20 + 25.20 = $28.40. Using only 11 kilometres of charges gives $26.30, and leaving out the flag fall gives $25.20.

questions.stem: A taxi charges a flag fall of $3.20 plus $2.10 per kilometre. The longest whole-kilometre trip a passenger can afford with $40 is:
questions.explanation: Solve 3.20 + 2.10n ≤ 40: 2.10n ≤ 36.80, so n ≤ 17.5. A 17 km trip costs $38.90 and an 18 km trip costs $41.00, which is more than $40.

questions.stem: $8000 is invested at 4.5% per annum simple interest. The interest earned each year is:
questions.explanation: Simple interest is the same every year: 8000 × 0.045 = $360. This constant amount is the common difference of the arithmetic sequence of balances.

questions.stem: $8000 is invested at 4.5% per annum simple interest. Its value after 5 years is:
questions.explanation: Each year adds 8000 × 0.045 = $360, so after 5 years the value is 8000 + 5 × 360 = $9800. $9969.46 is what compound interest would give, which is a geometric model.

questions.stem: A simple interest investment is modelled by the sequence 5000, 5225, 5450, 5675, ... (balance at the start of each year). The annual interest rate is:
questions.explanation: The common difference is 5225 − 5000 = $225 per year, and 225 ÷ 5000 = 0.045, which is 4.5%. With simple interest the yearly interest is always a percentage of the original principal.

questions.stem: Straight-line depreciation is modelled by an arithmetic sequence because the asset's value:
options: decreases by the same percentage each year
increases by the same amount each year
decreases by a larger amount each year
decreases by the same amount each year
questions.explanation: With the straight-line method the value falls by a fixed dollar amount each year, so the values form an arithmetic sequence with a negative common difference. A fixed percentage decrease is the diminishing-value method.

questions.stem: A car bought for $30 000 depreciates by $2500 per year using the straight-line method. If t₁ = 30 000 is the purchase price, the term that gives its value after 4 years, and that value, are:
questions.explanation: With t₁ as the purchase price, the value after n years is tₙ₊₁. After 4 years: t₅ = 30 000 + 4 × (−2500) = $20 000. t₄ is the value after only 3 years, $22 500.

questions.stem: A machine bought for $30 000 depreciates by $2500 per year using the straight-line method. After how many years will its value be $5000?
questions.explanation: The value must fall by 30 000 − 5000 = $25 000, and 25 000 ÷ 2500 = 10 years. 12 years would be the time to reach zero, which is 30 000 ÷ 2500.

questions.stem: A machine was bought for $18 000. Using straight-line depreciation, its value after 6 years is $6000. The annual depreciation is:
questions.explanation: The value fell by 18 000 − 6000 = $12 000 over 6 years, which is $2000 per year. Dividing the final value of $6000 by 6 gives $1000, which is not the yearly loss.

questions.stem: A geometric sequence is one in which:
options: the same number is added to each term to get the next term
each term is the sum of the two terms that come before it
the terms always increase by the same amount each time
each term is multiplied by the same number to get the next term
questions.explanation: A geometric sequence has a common ratio r, so each term is r times the one before it. Adding the same number each time gives an arithmetic sequence.

questions.stem: The common ratio of the geometric sequence 3, 6, 12, 24, ... is:
questions.explanation: The common ratio is any term divided by the term before it: 6 ÷ 3 = 2. Dividing the other way gives 0.5, and 3 is the common difference between the first two terms only.

questions.stem: The rule for the nth term of a geometric sequence with first term t₁ and common ratio r is:
questions.explanation: The first term has not been multiplied by r, the second has been multiplied once, and the nth term n − 1 times, so tₙ = t₁rⁿ⁻¹. Using rⁿ gives one multiplication too many.

questions.stem: For the geometric sequence 3, 6, 12, 24, ..., the 8th term is:
questions.explanation: t₈ = 3 × 2⁸⁻¹ = 3 × 128 = 384. Using 2⁸ gives 768, one doubling too many.

questions.stem: A sequence is defined by tₙ₊₁ = 0.8tₙ, t₁ = 500. The value of t₄ is:
questions.explanation: t₂ = 400, t₃ = 320, t₄ = 256 (or 500 × 0.8³ = 256). Applying 0.8 four times gives 204.8, which is t₅; subtracting 80 each time gives 260, an arithmetic slip.

questions.stem: Which of these is a geometric sequence?
questions.explanation: In 2, 6, 18, 54 each term is 3 times the one before, so the ratio is constant. 2, 6, 10, 14 has a common difference of 4 and is arithmetic; the other two have neither.

questions.stem: Which recursive definition generates the same sequence as tₙ = 5 × 2ⁿ⁻¹?
questions.explanation: The rule tₙ = 5 × 2ⁿ⁻¹ has first term 5 and common ratio 2, so each term is twice the last, starting at 5. Starting at 10 would make every term double what it should be.

questions.stem: A geometric sequence has t₂ = 6 and t₅ = 162. The first term is:
questions.explanation: From t₂ to t₅ is 3 multiplications, so r³ = 162 ÷ 6 = 27 and r = 3. Then t₁ = t₂ ÷ r = 6 ÷ 3 = 2. Multiplying t₂ by r instead of dividing gives 18, which is t₃.

questions.stem: When the terms of a geometric sequence with common ratio 1.5 are graphed against the term number, the points:
options: rise by the same amount each time, showing linear growth
fall more and more slowly, showing exponential decay
lie on a straight line that passes through the origin
rise more and more steeply, showing exponential growth
questions.explanation: With r greater than 1 each term grows by a larger amount than the last, so the points curve upwards, which is exponential growth. A ratio between 0 and 1 would give decay that flattens out.

questions.stem: An item loses 12% of its value each year. In the recursion tₙ₊₁ = rtₙ, the value of r is:
questions.explanation: Losing 12% leaves 100% − 12% = 88% of the value each year, so r = 0.88. Using 0.12 would keep only the amount lost, and 1.12 would model 12% growth.

questions.stem: A bacterial population doubles every hour. It starts with 200 bacteria. How many are there after 6 hours?
questions.explanation: After 6 doublings the population is 200 × 2⁶ = 12 800. With t₁ = 200 at the start, this is t₇; using t₆ gives 6400, which is after only 5 hours.

questions.stem: A $40 000 car depreciates by 15% per year using the diminishing-value method. Its value after 3 years is:
questions.explanation: Each year the value is multiplied by 0.85, so after 3 years it is 40 000 × 0.85³ = $24 565. Taking 45% off the original price gives $22 000, which treats the depreciation as straight-line.

questions.stem: A $40 000 car depreciates by 15% per year using the diminishing-value method. After how many whole years is its value first below $20 000?
questions.explanation: The values at the end of each year are $34 000, $28 900, $24 565, $20 880.25 and $17 748.21. After 4 years it is still just above $20 000, so it first drops below after 5 years.

questions.stem: A town's population of 12 000 grows by 5% each year. Its population after 3 years, to the nearest whole number, is:
questions.explanation: Geometric growth multiplies by 1.05 each year: 12 000 × 1.05³ = 13 891.5, which rounds to 13 892. Adding 5% of 12 000 each year gives 13 800, which is linear growth.

questions.stem: A $20 000 machine can be depreciated by $3000 per year (straight-line) or by 20% per year (diminishing-value). Which is correct?
options: After 2 years the straight-line value is higher; after 5 years the diminishing-value value is higher
After 2 years the diminishing-value value is higher; after 5 years the straight-line value is higher
The straight-line value is higher after both 2 years and 5 years, because $3000 is less than 20%
The diminishing-value value is higher after both 2 years and 5 years, because it never reaches zero
questions.explanation: After 2 years: straight-line $14 000, diminishing-value 20 000 × 0.8² = $12 800. After 5 years: straight-line $5000, diminishing-value 20 000 × 0.8⁵ = $6553.60. The diminishing-value loss shrinks each year, so the curve eventually stays above the straight line.

questions.stem: An asset worth $50 000 is worth $40 000 one year later and $32 000 the year after. Which model fits these values, and what is the value after 3 years?
questions.explanation: The changes are −10 000 then −8000, so the difference is not constant, but 40 000 ÷ 50 000 = 32 000 ÷ 40 000 = 0.8, so the model is geometric. After 3 years the value is 32 000 × 0.8 = $25 600; $20 480 is one more year on.

questions.stem: A table of values starts at 64 and each value is 1.5 times the one before. The 4th value in the table is:
questions.explanation: The values are 64, 96, 144, 216, or t₄ = 64 × 1.5³ = 216. 144 is the third value and 324 is the fifth.

questions.stem: Simple interest growth and diminishing-value depreciation are modelled, in that order, by:
options: a geometric sequence and another geometric one
an arithmetic sequence and a geometric sequence
a geometric sequence and an arithmetic sequence
an arithmetic sequence and another arithmetic one
questions.explanation: Simple interest adds the same dollar amount each period, which is arithmetic (linear) growth. Diminishing-value depreciation removes the same percentage each period, which is geometric (exponential) decay.

questions.stem: An item's value at the start of each year is $12 000, $10 800, $9720, ... The depreciation method and rate are:
questions.explanation: The ratios 10 800 ÷ 12 000 and 9720 ÷ 10 800 both equal 0.9, so the value keeps 90% and loses 10% each year. The drops are $1200 then $1080, which are not equal, so it is not straight-line.
